title: Greatest Common Divisor Traversal
summary: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums, you can traverse between indices i and j if the greatest common divisor of nums[i] and nums[j] is greater than 1.
statement: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums, you can traverse between indices i and j if the greatest common divisor of nums[i] and nums[j] is greater than 1. Determine if every pair of indices i < j can be connected through a sequence of such traversals. Return true if all pairs can be connected, otherwise return false.
constraints: Indices i and j have a direct traversal edge when gcd(nums[i],nums[j]) is greater than one.
Determine whether every index belongs to one connected component through any number of traversal edges.
Return True for a one-element array and False when a larger array contains one.
hints: Factor every value into distinct prime factors.
Use a disjoint-set structure to join indices sharing an already-seen prime owner.
After processing all factors, verify every index has the same representative.
Two values have gcd greater than one exactly when they share a prime, and union transitivity exactly matches paths of allowed traversals.
editorial: Two values have gcd greater than one exactly when they share a prime, and union transitivity exactly matches paths of allowed traversals.
